chunks: And Mas'adah ibn Sadaqah al-Raba'i narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) said: "The bequest (al-wasiyyah) is the completion of what is lacking from the alms-tax (zakat)."

key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: Alms-tax; the obligatory annual payment of a specific portion of wealth to the poor and needy.
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةُ: Bequest; the obligatory leaving of one-third of an estate to non-heirs or for charitable causes.
key_terms.عَلِيٌّ: Ali ibn Abi Talib, the first Imam.

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between bequest (wasiyyah) and alms-tax (zakat) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Mas‘adah ibn Sadqa narrates from Imam Ja‘far al-Sadiq that Imam Ali (peace be upon him) defines the bequest (al-wasiyyah) as the completion of what is lacking in zakat, highlighting its role in perfecting one's financial worship. This hadith underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that while zakat is obligatory, the bequest serves as a crucial mechanism for distributing wealth to the poor and specific beneficiaries, thereby fulfilling the broader social and spiritual objectives of charity beyond the fixed rates of zakat.
